articles.title: 'It felt like I was dying’: Why some teenagers don’t go to school
articles.summary: Teenagers speak to the BBC about struggling with school anxiety ahead of a landmark report on youth unemployment.
articles.body:
Thousands of school pupils in England miss more than half the academic year, which experts say puts them more at risk of becoming Neet - not in employment, education or training.

A government-commissioned review into how to solve the problem of nearly one million young people being Neet is due to be published on Tuesday.

Two teenagers who experience school anxiety have spoken to the BBC about what led them to stop attending classes.

Mali, 18, is autistic and stopped going to school three years ago after experiencing panic attacks. She said leaving her bedroom would make her legs go numb.

"It felt like I was dying," she told the BBC.

Thirteen-year-old Eva, who is also autistic, stopped going to school after struggling with the transition to secondary education.

"It's like a physical barrier that you can't cross and you can't move," she said.

articles.title: Simple Plan plays in-flight concert on one of the last trips out before FAA ground stop: 'We got really lucky'
articles.summary: The Canadian rockers and two other 2000s bands — Hoobastank and The Used — performed for passengers before the U.S.-wide ground stop.
articles.body:
Shortly before a nationwide ground stop in the United States led to a weekend of travel chaos, some lucky passengers were treated to some unexpected in-flight entertainment.

On Friday, travellers on a Southwest Airlines flight from Los Angeles to Orlando witnessed a surprise concert by three bands from the early 2000s and a performance from a Canadian singer.

Clips surfaced on social media of the candid performances by Canadian rockers Simple Plan, along with Hoobastank and The Used. Toronto-bred singer LØLØ also sang, according to one video .

Hoobastank were first to perform with their hit "The Reason," and Simple Plan followed with renditions of "Perfect" and "I'm Just a Kid." The Used then closed out the no-frills concert by performing "The Taste of Ink."

"Now that's what I call in-flight entertainment," Jordan Orion, a passenger on the flight, wrote in a social media clip that featured other fliers filming and raising their hands to the bands performing.

"We got really lucky," Orion told Daily Voice .

People online were loving the mid-flight show, with many expressing awe over the once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.

"It was the best flight ever!" Chuck Comeau, Simple Plan's drummer, penned on one video.

"I'm crying, I would've literally loved to be there," another raved .

"This is so freaking cool are you joking," someone wrote on a video of Hoobastank's performance.

"God, I've seen what you've done for others," someone else quipped on a clip featuring The Used's performance.

"The dream flight!!! So amazing," someone shared on another video of Simple Plan frontman Pierre Bouvier singing "I'm Just a Kid."

According to LØLØ, the flight was a "special chartered flight" full of people headed to the Vans Warped Tour, which is having its final 2026 stop from Nov. 14 to 15 in Florida. Southwest is the festival's airline partner, and its "Live at 35" program puts on "live music in the sky at 35,000 feet," according to its YouTube channel .

"Every plane was grounded today, but the emo gods made sure this one flew," LØLØ, whose real name is Lauren Mandel, wrote on her Instagram Stories.

"The craziest flight," she added in another post's caption.

The mid-flight performances took place before the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered all departing flights across the country to remain on the ground on Friday. Thousands of flights to and from the U.S. were impacted, with ripple effects continuing into Saturday .

Canada's major airports also saw disruptions on Friday , with many flights suspended and Nav Canada warning travellers to expect delays. The agency implemented traffic management measures at Toronto Pearson and Montreal-Trudeau, along with the international airports in Calgary and Vancouver.

On Friday, the FAA reopened the airspace at 8:15 p.m., about four hours after the initial outage reports. Officials shared updates on the situation Saturday, with U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blaming contractor L3Harris for the outage.

The FAA said schedules should be back to normal by the end of Sunday, but thousands more flights to and from the U.S. were impacted on Saturday.

articles.title: A hotel in Germany reports Chlorine gas poisoning after email warning system fails due to Microsoft 365 outage; guests taken to hospital
articles.summary: The recent 24-hour-plus Microsoft cloud outage reportedly prevented an automated safety system from alerting staff to a chemical malfunction at a German
articles.body: The recent 24-hour-plus Microsoft cloud outage reportedly prevented an automated safety system from alerting staff to a chemical malfunction at a German theme park hotel. The incident led to a Chlorine gas leak that injured 15 people, local broadcaster WDR reported. The incident occurred in the pool and sauna area of the Hotel Ling Bao at the Phantasialand theme park in Bruhl. According to emergency services, a defect in the pool’s automatic dosing system caused excessive amounts of chlorine to be pumped into the water, triggering a hazardous gas leak.The facility’s maintenance safety system is designed to monitor chemical levels and notify staff of irregularities via email. However, when the system attempted to dispatch a warning regarding the surging chlorine levels, the Outlook message failed to arrive due to widespread disruptions affecting Microsoft’s Exchange cloud infrastructure. Without the automated alert, the chemical buildup went undetected until guests and staff began experiencing symptoms.A total of 40 first responders were reportedly dispatched to the scene. According to the local fire department, 15 individuals suffered respiratory irritation and required emergency triage. Four people were transported to nearby hospitals for further treatment, with one patient remaining hospitalized under observation. Subsequent testing by emergency crews confirmed that the malfunctioning dosing mechanism had pushed the pool's chlorine concentrations to dangerously high levels.Microsoft's longest outageMicrosoft outage, reports of which started climbing around ⁠1725 GMT on November 12 according to Ookla, is one of the longest in the company's history. The outage prevented people from performing essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars and hosting virtual ​meetings. As Microsoft Outlook and Teams are two of the most widely used workplace applications with hundreds of millions of users. Microsoft said the outage specifically hit features tied to Exchange Online — its cloud-based email and ​scheduling hub — leaving unconnected applications operational.The outage affected government agencies from Australia and Japan to the United States, caused delays at trading firms, hindered some companies from publishing earnings and prompted airlines to warn customers of communication lags, according to ​public statements. Downdetector logged more than 7.4 million reports worldwide, peaking at nearly 20,000 a minute, more than 1,500 times normal levels.This was the second big outage for the company this year. Microsoft also faced an outage with its 365 services in January this year and in ‌ October last year. articles.title: Única no país, escultura missioneira de mais de 3 séculos é restaurada | G1
articles.standfirst: Imagem de São João Evangelista estava coberta por tinta em museu. Restauro revelou abertura secreta usada na tradição católica para guardar ossos e tecidos de santos.
articles.summary: Imagem de São João Evangelista estava coberta por tinta em museu. Restauro revelou abertura secreta usada na tradição católica para guardar ossos e tecidos de santos.
articles.body:
Uma escultura missioneira com mais de 300 anos , considerada a única relíquia desse tipo conhecida no Rio Grande do Sul e no Brasil , foi restaurada e voltará a integrar o patrimônio da Paróquia de São Pedro do Sul, na Região Central do estado. Trata-se da figura de São João Evangelista.

A peça estava guardada na reserva técnica do Museu Paleontológico e Arqueológico Walter Ilha e passou por um trabalho de identificação e restauro. Segundo o responsável pelo processo, a imagem estava completamente coberta por camadas de tinta, que escondiam características originais da obra.

"É a única escultura de relíquia missioneira de mais de 300 anos no RS e Brasil", define o professor Édison Hüttner, da pós-graduação em História e em Teologia da PCURS.

Durante a restauração, foi descoberta uma abertura móvel no centro da escultura . Segundo o professor, o compartimento era utilizado para guardar relíquias religiosas, como fragmentos de tecidos ou de ossos de santos, prática comum na tradição católica .

Um detalhe permitiu identificar o santo representado na peça: foi a posição dos pés sobre um livro apoiado em uma montanha. Os elementos remetem à Ilha de Patmos e ao Livro do Apocalipse, associados a São João Evangelista , que, segundo a tradição cristã, teria escrito o último livro da Bíblia durante o exílio na ilha grega.

Após a recuperação das características originais, a escultura será devolvida à Paróquia de São Pedro do Sul, proprietária da obra, onde ficará novamente à disposição da comunidade religiosa e dos visitantes.

A restauração também revelou detalhes artísticos e históricos que estavam ocultos, reforçando a importância da peça para o patrimônio missioneiro e religioso do estado.

articles.title: Conheça memorial que eterniza legados de missionários no Pará | G1
articles.standfirst: Localizado em Belém, memorial “Três vidas, uma causa” reúne imagens, premiações e objetos pessoais dos três missionários que foram símbolo da luta em defesa dos direitos humanos.
articles.summary: Localizado em Belém, memorial “Três vidas, uma causa” reúne imagens, premiações e objetos pessoais dos três missionários que foram símbolo da luta em defesa dos direitos humanos
articles.body:
As trajetórias marcadas pela fé e pelo ativismo em defesa dos mais vulneráveis de três missionários foram reúnidas e eternizadas no memorial “Três vidas, uma causa”, do Instituto Dom Luiz Azcona, em Belém .

O espaço celebra os legados de irmã Henriqueta Cavalcante, padre Bruno Secchi e dom Luiz Azcona, que promoveram avanços na busca por direitos humanos, principalmente para crianças e adolescentes no Pará.

"O nome do memorial já diz muita coisa: Envolve três missionários extretamente importantes para a defesa dos direitos humanos. Decidimos fazer essa homenagem, contando um pouco da história porque o trabalho prossegue, dos três missionários", detalha Mary Cohen, presidente do Instituto Dom Azcona.

O espaço reúne fotos, premiações e objetos pessoais dos homenageados. Do guarda-roupa da irmã, por exemplo, há blusas de campanhas que ela apoiou e promoveu.

O memorial vai abrir para visitação do público na próxima quarta-feira (18), das 9h às 13h e das 14 às 18h, de segunda à sexta-feira. O local foi inaugurado em 11 de novembro, dia em que a irmã Henriqueta faria aniversário.

📍 O memorial “Três vidas, uma causa” fica na nova sede do Instituto Dom Luiz Azcona (Idah), na sede do Centro de Defesa da Criança e Adolescente (Cedeca-Emaús), na Travessa Dom Romualdo de Seixas, 918, bairro do Umarizal, em Belém.

Memorial homenageia Dom Azcona, Irmã Henriqueta e Padre Bruno Sechi — Foto: Edenilton Marques/TV Liberal

Padre Bruno, irmã Henriqueta e dom Azcona construíram um trabalho que segue vivo pelas mãos de quem dá continuidade a suas lutas pelos mais vulneráveis. No Instituto Dom Azcona, por exemplo, há um espaço de escuta e acolhimento que recebe denúncias de violações de direitos humanos. O local funciona como uma ponte entre a sociedade civil e o poder público.

Henriqueta morreu em janeiro de 2026 em um acidente de carro na Paraíba. Ela e Dom Azcona se tornaram símbolos da luta contra a exploração sexual infantil no arquipélago do Marajó.

Irmã Henriqueta lutou contra o abuso infantil no Marajó e morreu em 2026 — Foto: Reprodução / TV Liberal

Irmã Henriqueta era defensora dos direitos humanos e ativista desde 2009. Ao longo de seu trabalho, sofreu ameaças de morte. Por isso, estava incluída no programa de proteção para defensores dos direitos humanos há mais de uma década.

Em novembro de 2025, irmã Henriqueta foi uma das premiadas na edição especial Amazônia do " Mulheres Inspiradoras do Ano" . O trabalho de irmã Henriqueta contra a violência no Marajó também foi inspiração para o filme Manas . A religiosa também foi membro da Comissão de Justiça e Paz da Conferência Nacional dos Bispos do Brasil (CNBB).

Irmã Henriqueta presidiu até o início de 2026 o Instituto de Direitos Humanos Dom José Luis Azcona, que leva o nome do bispo emérito do Marajó que morreu em 2024 . Ele e irmã Henriqueta Cavalcante lutaram contra a exploração e o tráfico sexual de crianças e mulheres marajoaras.

Dom Azcona foi símbolo da luta dos direitos humanos no arquipélago do Marajó e morreu em 2024 — Foto: CNBB/Divulgação

Dom Luiz Azcona era espanhol e missionário. Como bispo do Marajó desde a década de 1980, o religioso denunciou a miséria e a devastação ambiental no arquipélago.

O trabalho na defesa dos direitos humanos no Marajó fez com que, em 2008, o nome dele estivesse entre lideranças católicas ameaçadas de morte no Pará.

O bispo emérito foi fundamental para a instalação da CPI da Pedofilia na Assembleia Legislativa do Pará e no Congresso Nacional. Além disso, em 2015, ele denunciou casos em que crianças foram exploradas por visitantes que chegavam à região.

Henriqueta também era amiga de padre Bruno Secchi, criador da República do Emaús, que morre em 2020 aos 80 anos por complicações da Covid-19 .

Padre Bruno Sechi morreu em 2020 — Foto: Akira Onuma

Na década de 1970, ele alavancou trabalhos com crianças em situação de rua em Belém. A atuação levou à criação do movimento República de Emaús, que leva educação profissional, cultural e cidadã à comunidade.

Na década de 80, padre Bruno também participou das ações políticas no Brasil que culminaram na criação do Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente (ECA). Em 2021, suas obras sociais foram reunidas no Memorial Padre Bruno Sechi.

articles.title: Grilagem no Amazonas: estradas e falta de análise do CAR geram alerta | G1
articles.standfirst: Alerta ocorre após dados do MapBiomas mostrarem que, embora o Amazonas ainda mantenha 94,6% da vegetação nativa preservada, regiões de fronteira agrícola enfrentam pressão crescente de atividades agropecuárias.
articles.summary: Especialistas alertam que a falta de análise do Cadastro Ambiental Rural e o asfaltamento de rodovias facilitam a grilagem e o desmatamento no Amazonas.
articles.body:
A abertura e o asfaltamento de rodovias no Amazonas podem facilitar a grilagem de terras públicas e a especulação imobiliária, além de ampliar o desmatamento. Segundo especialistas em governança territorial e direito ambiental ouvidos pelo g1 , o avanço das obras precisa ser acompanhado de medidas de ordenamento fundiário, fiscalização e análise dos registros de propriedades rurais para evitar a ocupação irregular de áreas de floresta.

O alerta ocorre após dados do MapBiomas mostrarem que, embora o Amazonas ainda mantenha 94,6% da vegetação nativa preservada , regiões de fronteira agrícola, como a divisa entre Amazonas, Acre e Rondônia (AMACRO), enfrentam pressão crescente de atividades agropecuárias.

Para Heron Martins, diretor executivo do Instituto Dados e integrante do comitê técnico do Observatório do Código Florestal, um dos principais problemas é a existência de terras públicas sem destinação definida .

"As estradas reduzem o custo de acesso à terra e de escoamento da produção. O que determina se esse acesso se converte em desmatamento desordenado é a capacidade do Estado de ordenar o território. A ausência de destinação da terra, somada à facilidade de acesso pelas estradas, cria um ambiente favorável à especulação fundiária e a uma ocupação desordenada com o intuito de garantir um direito futuro sobre a terra", explica Martins.

O doutor em Ciências do Ambiente e doutorando em Direito Ambiental pela Universidade do Estado do Amazonas ( UEA ), Antonio Norte, também avalia que a abertura de estradas precisa estar vinculada ao planejamento territorial e à fiscalização ambiental .

"A infraestrutura não pode ser utilizada como justificativa para flexibilizar indiscriminadamente a proteção ambiental. Nas faixas de domínio rodoviário e em seus entornos, o desafio é transformar a proteção prevista em lei em presença efetiva do Estado, com monitoramento por satélite, fiscalização integrada, responsabilização dos infratores e atuação preventiva. A estrada não pode funcionar como vetor de ocupação desordenada, mas como infraestrutura submetida ao planejamento territorial e à responsabilidade ambiental", destaca Norte.

Cadastro Ambiental Rural sem análise facilita ocupações irregulares

Criado pelo Código Florestal de 2012, o Cadastro Ambiental Rural (CAR) reúne informações ambientais das propriedades e posses rurais do país. Na Amazônia, porém, o instrumento também tem sido usado de forma irregular .

Segundo especialistas, registros feitos pelos próprios declarantes, sem análise e validação dos órgãos responsáveis, podem ser utilizados para simular a posse de terras e tentar legitimar a ocupação de áreas públicas federais e estaduais.

Para evitar esse tipo de prática, Martins defende que os órgãos públicos ampliem a análise dos cadastros e cancelem os registros irregulares.

"É necessário que, além do cadastramento, ocorra um esforço de análise e validação do CAR para que cadastros indevidos sejam cancelados rapidamente, reduzindo a expectativa indevida de posse. As áreas de Reserva Legal e APP precisam ser aprovadas, formando corredores com as áreas protegidas", pontua o especialista.

Incra identifica 3,1 milhões de hectares de terras públicas sem destinação no Sul do AM

Ao g1 , o Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária (Incra) informou que uma base cartográfica de 2024 identificou cerca de 3,1 milhões de hectares de terras públicas federais sem destinação em oito municípios do Sul do Amazonas.

As áreas estão distribuídas entre Apuí , Boca do Acre , Canutama , Humaitá , Lábrea , Manicoré , Novo Aripuanã e Pauini .

Segundo o Incra, as terras foram analisadas pela Câmara Técnica de Destinação e Regularização Fundiária de Terras Públicas Federais Rurais (CTD), coordenada pelo Ministério do Desenvolvimento Agrário e Agricultura Familiar (MDA).

Após a análise, órgãos federais manifestaram interesse em utilizar as áreas para diferentes finalidades. Veja a distribuição:

Ministério do Meio Ambiente (MMA);1.183.447,63 hectares;

Incra (Regularização Fundiária):1.236.623,85 hectares;

Funai (Terras Indígenas):240.192,85 hectares;.

Funai (Área sobreposta/conjunta): 219.103,53 hectares

AMACRO concentra pressão sobre terras públicas

A região conhecida como AMACRO, na divisa entre o Sul do Amazonas, o Acre e Rondônia , concentra parte da pressão sobre a floresta no estado. Municípios como Lábrea, Apuí e Humaitá aparecem com frequência entre os que registram os maiores índices de desmatamento no Amazonas.

Diferentemente de outras áreas do estado, o Sul do Amazonas tem uma grande quantidade de terras públicas sem destinação definida, ou seja, áreas que ainda não foram destinadas a unidades de conservação, terras indígenas ou outras finalidades legais.

Sem uma definição sobre o uso dessas terras pelo poder público, essas áreas ficam mais vulneráveis a invasões e loteamentos ilegais. A proximidade com rodovias e com áreas de produção agropecuária de estados vizinhos também facilita a ocupação.

Outro fator é a abertura de ramais não oficiais, que são estradas secundárias construídas sem autorização. Essas vias podem conectar áreas de pastagem ao interior da floresta, facilitando o avanço do desmatamento.

A abertura de estradas também pode provocar o chamado efeito de borda, que altera as condições ambientais nas áreas próximas à floresta desmatada . Entre as consequências estão mudanças no microclima, maior risco de queimadas e fragmentação de habitats, inclusive no entorno de terras indígenas e unidades de conservação.

Falta de integração entre cartórios e órgãos ambientais

A falta de comunicação entre os sistemas de controle de terras e os órgãos ambientais também é apontada como um obstáculo à fiscalização.

Sem o cruzamento de informações dos cartórios, dos cadastros fundiários e das bases ambientais, fica mais difícil identificar quem é o responsável por uma área e qual é a situação legal do terreno. Essa falta de integração também abre espaço para fraudes e registros sobrepostos em terras públicas ou áreas protegidas.

Antonio Norte afirma que a ausência de integração entre essas bases de dados favorece a grilagem na região.

"A principal fragilidade está na falta de integração entre os cadastros fundiários, os registros imobiliários e as bases de dados ambientais e territoriais. Quando não se consegue identificar com precisão a titularidade, a localização e a destinação de uma área pública, criam-se oportunidades para a grilagem e a sobreposição de registros", afirma Norte.

O pesquisador também ressalta que os processos de regularização fundiária não devem beneficiar quem ocupa terras públicas de forma ilegal ou comete crimes ambientais.

"A prioridade deve ser identificar, proteger e destinar adequadamente as terras públicas, distinguindo a ocupação legítima da apropriação irregular do patrimônio coletivo. Regularizar não significa legitimar a ocupação ilegal", reforça o doutorando da UEA.

articles.summary: O g1 compila concursos, processos seletivos e vagas de empregos com inscrições em andamento, contemplando diferentes áreas e níveis de escolaridade.
articles.body:
Oportunidades de emprego e de ingresso no serviço público estão abertas no Ceará, com vagas em Fortaleza e em outros municípios, nesta segunda-feira (16).

O g1 compila concursos, processos seletivos, cursos e vagas de empregos com inscrições em andamento, contemplando diferentes áreas e níveis de escolaridade.

Confira oportunidades no Ceará. — Foto: Freepik

Confira abaixo as oportunidades desta semana:

Formação em criação de jogos digitais no IFCE

O Instituto Federal do Ceará (IFCE) está com 500 vagas abertas para um programa gratuito de formação em desenvolvimento de jogos digitais . Os estudantes selecionados para a primeira etapa receberão bolsas mensais de R$ 700 durante três meses. As inscrições podem ser realizadas até 20 de novembro de 2026.

A capacitação será realizada a distância. Ao todo, serão 120 horas de formação, com conteúdos que vão desde a criação de personagens e cenários até programação, animação, produção de áudio e divulgação de jogos.

Podem participar estudantes regularmente matriculados em cursos técnicos de nível médio ou de graduação em áreas relacionadas à Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação (TIC), desde que morem em municípios do interior do Ceará.

A Prefeitura de Fortaleza está ofertando 792 vagas para cursos de idiomas do Instituto Municipal de Desenvolvimento de Recursos Humanos (Imparh). As oportunidades são para o semestre 2027.1 e contemplam sete línguas: alemão, espanhol, francês, inglês, italiano, japonês e português.

As inscrições devem ser feitas pela internet, até as 23h59 do dia 3 de janeiro de 2027, por meio do Canal de Concursos e Seleções da Prefeitura de Fortaleza . A taxa de inscrição é de R$ 95.

Para participar, os candidatos precisam ter, no mínimo, 14 anos e estar cursando ou já ter concluído o 9º ano do ensino fundamental.

Do total de vagas, 50% são destinadas prioritariamente a estudantes da rede pública de ensino, desde o último ano do ensino fundamental até o último ano do ensino médio.

A Prefeitura Municipal de Boa Viagem está com vagas abertas para um concurso público para cargos efetivos e formação de cadastro de reserva. Organizado pela Fundação Cetrede, o certame contempla oportunidades para profissionais de níveis fundamental incompleto, fundamental completo, médio e superior.

No total, o edital disponibiliza 1.001 vagas de início imediato e 2.002 vagas para formação de cadastro de reserva, totalizando 3.003 oportunidades

As inscrições serão efetuadas exclusivamente no site da Fundação Cetrede até 7 de dezembro de 2026.

O Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) oferta 1.527 vagas temporárias de recenseador no Ceará, para atuação no 12º Censo Agropecuário, Florestal e Aquícola.

Os interessados podem se inscrever até as 23h59 do dia 25 de novembro de 2026 , no site da Fundação Cesgranrio , com o pagamento da taxa de R$ 70.

Segundo o IBGE, os recenseadores receberão salário mensal de R$ 1.741, além de pagamento por produtividade. Também estão previstos benefícios como auxílio-alimentação de R$ 1.192, auxílio pré-escolar, 13º salário proporcional, férias proporcionais acrescidas de um terço constitucional e auxílio para custeio dos deslocamentos.

A Prefeitura de Fortaleza disponibiliza novas oportunidades de emprego por meio do Sine Municipal, reunindo um total de 2.827 vagas de emprego distribuídas em 296 empresas parceiras e contemplando 213 profissões . Os interessados devem procurar a unidade do Sine mais próxima.

As funções com maior número de vagas abertas na consulta atual são:

Operador de telemarketing ativo e receptivo: 606

Ajudante de carga e descarga de mercadoria: 87

A CR Duarte Engenharia está com 63 oportunidades de emprego em Fortaleza e Região Metropolitana na área da construção civil. A empresa busca novas contratações para as atividades de 2027, ano em que prevê iniciar sete novas obras.

Os cargos disponíveis abrangem diferentes áreas e níveis de formação, nas áreas técnica, administrativa e operacional.

Os interessados devem realizar a candidatura de forma online, até janeiro de 2027 , por meio de formulário eletrônico ( acesse aqui ). Os candidatos deverão preencher os dados de contato e enviar o currículo pela plataforma.

A Prefeitura de Fortaleza, em parceria com o CIEE, continua com inscrições abertas para o Programa de Jovens Talentos 2026 , que oferece vagas de estágio para estudantes do ensino médio, técnico e superior na administração pública municipal. As inscrições são gratuitas, seguem abertas até 31 de dezembro de 2026 e devem ser feitas exclusivamente pelo portal do CIEE .

Os estagiários recebem bolsa-auxílio de R$ 750 (ensino superior), R$ 550 (técnico) e R$ 450 (ensino médio), além de auxílio-transporte. A carga horária é de 4 horas diárias. Para participar, é preciso ter pelo menos 16 anos e estar regularmente matriculado em instituição reconhecida pelo MEC.

articles.title: Árvores ficaram mais fortes com menos poluição na pandemia, aponta USP | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa do Cena/USP, sediado em Piracicaba (SP), mostra que o ar mais limpo na pandemia deixou a madeira mais densa. Com a estrutura mais estável, diminui o risco de quedas e acidentes urbanos.
articles.summary: Pesquisa do Cena/USP, sediado em Piracicaba (SP), mostra que o ar mais limpo na pandemia deixou a madeira mais densa. Com a estrutura mais estável, diminui o risco de quedas.
articles.body:
Avenida 23 de Maio, Zona Sul de São Paulo — Foto: FÁBIO VIEIRA/FOTORUA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

Cientistas investigaram como a queda brusca da poluição durante os lockdowns da pandemia de Covid-19 afetou as árvores urbanas em São Paulo (SP). O estudo mostrou que o ar mais limpo fez com que as árvores urbanas ficassem com a madeira mais densa, o que as deixou mais estáveis e resistentes. O fato contribui para a diminuição de quedas de árvores e acidentes urbanos (entenda mais abaixo).

A pesquisa foi liderada pelo pós-doutorando Augusto Akio Lucchezi Miyahara, do Centro de Energia Nuclear na Agricultura (Cena), instituto de pesquisa em Piracicaba (SP) vinculado à Universidade de São Paulo (USP), e orientada por Giuliano Maselli Locosselli.

"No planeta, nunca houve um outro momento em que houve uma redução da poluição do ar consistente em diferentes lugares do mundo. A gente tem eventos que mudam a composição da atmosfera, mas, no geral, para pior", conta Locosselli.

A pesquisa integra o projeto Florestas Funcionais, financiado pela Fundação Paulista de Amparo à Pesquisa (FAPESP), e foi publicada na revista internacional Environmental Pollution.

O estudo analisou exemplares de tipuana (Tipuana Tipo) da Avenida 23 de Maio e do Parque Ibirapuera. A ideia era analisar como a falta de poluição afetou as árvores que são mais e menos expostas à poluição.

Os pesquisadores observaram diferenças entre os locais analisados. As árvores da Avenida 23 de Maio, mais expostas ao tráfego intenso, tiveram aumento expressivo na densidade da madeira durante as semanas de lockdown.

Já no Parque Ibirapuera, usado como área de controle por ter menor exposição à fumaça dos veículos, essa mudança brusca não foi registrada.

"Não vimos a mudança [na madeira] nas árvores do parque, porque também não vimos mudança na questão da poluição. A mudança mais aguda não ocorreu porque o parque não está exposto aos poluentes como a avenida", informa Miyahara.

Tipuanas na Avenida Cruzeiro do Sul, em Piracicaba — Foto: Yasmin Moscoski/g1

Para analisar as árvores sem derrubá-las, os cientistas retiraram pequenos cilindros de madeira do tronco com uma broca oca com o intuito de ter acesso a um trecho dos anéis de crescimento de uma árvore. Locosselli explicou que o procedimento foi semelhante a uma 'biópsia' nos anéis de crescimento.

Anéis de crescimento: ao cortar o tronco de uma árvore, é possível notar que ela possui círculos concêntricos (como um alvo de arco e flecha ou ondulações na água). Esses círculos representam a idade da árvore, além de indicarem condições do clima que aquela árvore presenciou, como secas, chuvas abundantes, incêndios e poluição.

O principal diferencial do estudo foi a precisão das análises. Em vez de observar apenas o crescimento anual por meio dos anéis de crescimento, como é mais comum, os pesquisadores dividiram o anel de crescimento de um único ano em 15 partes.

Para fazer essa análise minuciosa, contaram com o apoio da ciência chilena. Assim, conseguiram acompanhar as respostas das árvores às mudanças de maneira semanal entre 2020 e 2021.

Cilindros de madeira do tronco — Foto: Divulgação/Instituto Mamirauá

Como a madeira ficou mais resistente e por que isso é importante

Com menos dióxido de carbono (CO₂) liberado pelos veículos no ar, a planta precisou abrir mais os estômatos, que são os poros das folhas, para captar o gás necessário à fotossíntese.

Os pesquisadores explicaram que, ao abrir mais esses poros, a árvore também perdeu mais água. Isso aumentou o risco de falhas no transporte interno de água. Como resposta, a passou a produzir madeira mais densa para evitar essas falhas.

"É um efeito colateral positivo. Quando você aumenta a densidade da madeira, ela fica mecanicamente mais estável", informa Locosselli.

Com árvores mais estáveis, diminui o índice de quedas e acidentes urbanos.

"Temos, realmente, que investir o máximo que a gente pode em redução da poluição do ar. Mas o interessante é que os benefícios se estendem não só à população, mas às árvores, que também trazem benefícios para a população", complementa o professor orientador.

O professor explicou ainda que, embora o CO₂ seja um insumo essencial para a fotossíntese, a poluição veicular das cidades não libera o CO₂ de forma isolada, mas acompanhado de uma série de elementos nocivos à saúde das plantas.

"As árvores diminuem até 30% a taxa de crescimento quando estão expostas a altas concentrações de poluentes", afirma.

A equipe também pretende ampliar o monitoramento de árvores em cidades médias, como Piracicaba. A ideia é mapear o comportamento da vegetação e ajudar na formulação de políticas de planejamento urbano e arborização.

articles.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu can’t remain Israel PM amid alleged vote meddling
articles.summary: Arab party members were reportedly arrested before Israeli elections based on unfounded evidence from the PM’s office.
articles.body:
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cannot “remain at the helm of government for even one more minute” amid reports alleging Netanyahu’s office engaged in electoral interference.

Eisenkot, tasked with forming Israel’s new government , launched a scathing attack on his rival on Sunday, just a few hours after representatives of the two men met to discuss the possible formation of a national unity government .

“The conduct of outgoing Prime Minister Netanyahu and his inner circle poses a tangible, direct and immediate threat to Israeli democracy,” Eisenkot wrote on X.

Israeli broadcaster Channel 12 published a report earlier on Sunday alleging Netanyahu’s chief of staff, Ido Norden, lodged a complaint with the police commissioner’s office against members of the United Arab List (Ra’am) party on the eve of Israel’s October 27 election .

Norden reportedly directed police officers to an alleged intelligence source who was a former employee of Netanyahu’s office.

Based on information from the source, about 14 police officers raided the homes of three Ra’am members without a warrant and arrested them on suspicion of bribery to incentivise voting, according to Channel 12.

Netanyahu subsequently launched a campaign against Arab-led parties throughout election day. After they won a record 19 seats, he made unproven accusations of electoral fraud.

The three men were released after police determined the information from the purported intelligence source was unfounded.

The Channel 12 report also alleged that David Zini, the head of Israel’s internal intelligence agency Shin Bet, requested the attorney general’s office to wiretap five Palestinian-Israeli Knesset members on election day over suspected election interference, but the request was later rejected.

“I call for an immediate investigation into the affair and for the police and the Shin Bet to immediately clarify the details that have been published,” said Eisenkot, a former army chief.

Netanyahu’s Likud party called Eisenkot’s statement “outrageous incitement” against the prime minister.

On Friday, Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of fuelling a “racist and violent” campaign against Palestinian citizens of Israel during the elections to cling to power.

Netanyahu renewed his appeal to Eisenkot to form a unity government on Saturday, but the opposition leader called the plea a “bluff”.

However, Eisenkot had confirmed talks between his Yashar party and the Likud party over the proposal for a shared government.

Neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot’s bloc has yet secured the 61 seats needed to form a government.

articles.title: Zambia’s copper boom attracts billions in investment, but who benefits?
articles.summary: Workers’ rights, environmental concerns and local businesses remain at the centre of the debate.
articles.body:
Lusaka, Zambia – Zambia is attracting billions of dollars in mining investment as it seeks to become a significant supplier of minerals critical to the global energy transition. But as foreign companies expand operations and new projects come on stream, questions are mounting over whether common Zambians are benefitting from the country’s growing mineral wealth.

President Hakainde Hichilema said more than $12bn had been invested in Zambia’s mining sector since 2022, as the government pushes to increase copper production and attract new investors.

Leading investors include Canadian companies First Quantum Minerals and Barrick Mining Corporation, India’s Vedanta Resources and China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group (CNMC).

Abu Dhabi-based International Resources Holding (IRH) has also emerged as a leading investor after committing $1.1bn to recapitalise Mopani Copper Mines, previously owned by Glencore. The investment gave IRH a 51 percent stake in the mine, with state-owned ZCCM Investments Holdings retaining 49 percent.

Alongside large-scale mining projects, the Copperbelt province has also seen the expansion of smaller Chinese-owned mineral-processing plants, some sourcing ore from artisanal and small-scale miners. Their growth has raised concerns about safety standards, regulatory oversight and environmental protection.

The government has sought to restore investor confidence through tax incentives and a more predictable fiscal framework, following years of frequent changes to mining tax policies under the former Patriotic Front government, which ruled Zambia between 2011 and 2021.

Unlocking mineral wealth and adding value

To accelerate mineral exploration, Zambia is undertaking a nationwide high-resolution aerial geophysical survey aimed at improving geological information and identifying previously unexplored mineral deposits. The survey is now about 98 percent complete, according to the Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development.

The government has set an ambitious target of increasing annual copper production to 3 million tonnes by 2031, from less than 1 million tonnes in recent years.

“We can do with our copper, cobalt, nickel, lithium, manganese and rare earth metals, which we now know we have in this country for our people, what the UAE has done with oil and gas for its people and their economy,” Hichilema told delegates at the Zambia Mining and Investment Forum in Lusaka on October 19.

Beyond increasing production, Zambia is also seeking to expand value addition to copper, a key material in electric vehicles and renewable energy infrastructure.

Historically, the country has exported copper cathodes to China and other industrialised countries. But the government wants Zambia to play a more active role in the global transition to a low-carbon economy by developing domestic mineral processing and manufacturing capacity.

Africa’s two leading copper producers, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Zambia, are also exploring a partnership with South Africa to develop an electric vehicle battery manufacturing industry.

“DRC and ourselves are doing something on EV materials so we can build a joint venture with South Africa, which is ahead of us in the motor industry, so that the motor vehicles produced out of South African production lines have Congolese and Zambian inputs of the EV battery,” Hichilema said.

The proposed partnership reflects growing efforts by African mineral producers to move beyond exporting raw materials and capture a greater share of the value generated by the global energy transition.

However, turning these ambitions into reality will require more than increased mineral production. It will also depend on the development of local industries, skilled labour and infrastructure capable of supporting large-scale manufacturing.

While foreign capital is driving an expansion of Zambia’s mining sector, trade unions say local workers are yet to see meaningful improvements in their working conditions.

“Inasmuch as the copper prices are going up and we have seen an increase in the amount of investments, we are experiencing same employment conditions – things are not any better for a mineworker,” Stephen Mwaanga, secretary of the National Union of Miners and Allied Workers, told Al Jazeera.

Despite higher copper prices, Mwaanga said, mining companies were also grappling with elevated production costs, including higher fuel prices, which he linked to the US-Israel war on Iran, affecting traffic via the Strait of Hormuz.

The wider Southern African region has also faced drought conditions associated with El Nino, putting additional pressure on electricity supplies. Zambia’s heavy reliance on hydropower makes the mining industry particularly vulnerable to reduced water levels, forcing the country to seek electricity imports and alternative sources of power.

Reliable electricity supplies are critical to sustaining the expansion of an industry that is central to Zambia’s economy.

“We need to strike a balance between improving the workers’ conditions of service and the challenges that these mining companies are facing,” Mwaanga said.

The challenge for the government is therefore not simply to attract more mining capital, but to ensure that increased production translates into better employment conditions and wider economic opportunities for Zambians.

Beyond workers’ welfare, the rapid expansion of mining is raising concerns about its environmental consequences, particularly in communities already affected by pollution.

Eugene Mulenga, a human rights defender, fears the government’s drive to increase mineral production could place enormous pressure on the environment.

In February 2025, a structural failure at a tailings dam operated by Chinese-owned Sino-Metals Leach Zambia in Copperbelt released acidic, metal-laden mining waste into the Chambishi Stream. The pollution spread downstream into the Mwambashi and Kafue river systems, raising serious concerns about water quality, aquatic life and the livelihoods of communities dependent on the waterways.

A subsequent environmental assessment by the Zambia Environmental Management Agency documented the extent of the ecological damage and the effects of the discharge on affected waterways.

The incident exposed the environmental risks associated with mining expansion and renewed questions about the ability of regulatory authorities to monitor operations and enforce environmental standards.

Other pollution incidents have also been reported at mining operations, adding to concerns about the industry’s environmental footprint.

Zambia’s push to increase copper production to 3 million tonnes annually by 2031 has therefore intensified calls for stronger environmental safeguards and greater accountability from mining companies.

For common Zambians and local businesses, the benefits of the country’s growing mining investments also remain a subject of debate.

In an effort to ensure more mining-related spending circulates within the domestic economy, the government introduced local-content regulations, which require mining companies to allocate at least 20 percent of their annual procurement budgets for core mining goods and services to local suppliers in 2026. The threshold is scheduled to rise to 25 percent after one year, with further increases planned.

The policy is intended to strengthen indigenous businesses, create opportunities for Zambian suppliers and ensure a greater share of economic benefits from mining remains within the country.

But as Zambia positions itself to become a key supplier of minerals critical to the global energy transition, the question remains whether the investment boom will deliver meaningful improvements in citizens’ lives, particularly those living and working in mining communities.

For Mulenga, the economic ambitions must not come at the expense of communities whose livelihoods depend on the environment.

“What we have discovered is that most farmers and poor people who depend directly on these water bodies near the mining sites are being affected by the increasing mining activity,” he told Al Jazeera.

articles.title: Town destroyed by flood rebuilt by Libya's strongman Khalifa Haftar - but questions remain
articles.summary: The remarkable reconstruction of Derna is being used as a showcase for the rest of Libya by Khalifa Haftar and his sons.
articles.body:
"It was joy when I moved in. I could finally relax," says Abdulwahab Damdoum, surveying his luxurious new apartment overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, in the eastern Libyan city of Derna.

Just three years ago he was clinging in terror to the roof of a house as the world's deadliest flood this century surged around him.

Now the 27-year-old port worker, his wife and two young daughters have been given a new, free, 300-sq-m home in a showcase development commissioned by a son of Khalifa Haftar, the warlord who controls eastern Libya.

It is part of a rapid $2bn (£1.5bn) rebuilding of Derna that the powerful Haftar family hope will serve as a model for development throughout Libya, increasing their influence across a country currently split between east and west, with rival governments in charge.

The money comes from the state coffers of the oil-rich country, allocated by its parliament. But there are no published records of how it has been spent, raising questions about accountability and possible corruption.

Damdoum, like many flood survivors, simply thanks the head of the Development and Reconstruction Fund, Belkacem Haftar, for what has been achieved since the early hours of 11 September 2023, when lashing rain from Storm Daniel burst two dams above Derna, sending a wall of water 7m (23 ft) high cascading down onto the sleeping city.

The exact death toll will probably never be known. Some estimates have been as high as 6,000, though 4,000 now seems a more likely figure. Many bodies are still unidentified.

In a city of about 100,000 people, that means almost everybody lost someone they loved. The 14 relatives and neighbours on the roof with Damdoum – including his father, brother and sister - all drowned.

He survived, but his home was destroyed, and he had to find temporary accommodation. "It was rent, rent, rent," he says. "Now, no-one can take this [new flat] from me. I thank Engineer Belkacem. God sent this person who picked the city up from disaster."

Portraits of Belkacem, widely known simply as "the Engineer", his younger brother Saddam, a military chief also involved in reconstruction, and their father Khalifa are on hoardings all over Derna and the region.

"Since 2011, Libya has not built big projects like this," says Hussein el-Mansory, project manager of the "2,000 Apartments" complex where Damdoum now lives. "I feel very happy and proud and I'll tell my children: 'I made this.'"

The complex includes a new mosque, hospital, shopping mall and schools. New roads, bridges have also been built in Derna. But while many survivors have been rehoused, some are still waiting.

Among them is Izz al-Nasr Ibzeou, a marine science lecturer at the university. His wife Salima, her mother Mouna, and all the couple's seven children, aged between one and 11, drowned.

His family home was ruined, but the authorities have not yet fully restored it because Ibzeou also has an undamaged apartment in another part of town.

He returns every day to his old house, now an empty shell, to see his children's possessions, which he has kept in dust-covered piles.

"This is my son Moez's bike. He played with it every day. And this is my daughter Fawzia's dress. She wore it whenever she went to a wedding," Ibzeou says. "Even if I decide not to come to remember them, my feet will bring me here of their own accord."

To this day, he has not found their bodies. In Derna's vast new flood cemetery, most graves are marked only by numbers, not names, because the process of matching survivors' DNA with corpses is still not completed.

"I go to the cemetery and try to guess where my family are," he says. "This has burned my heart too much. Thank God, I'm patient, but I'm still waiting just to read the Qur'an [at their graves] and say hello to them."

Belkacem Haftar has now extended the work of his reconstruction fund to Libya's second city, Benghazi, and other parts of Libya his father controls.

Libya's parliament, based in the east, last year allocated him a further sum of nearly $11bn, to be spent over three years, in addition to the $2bn it had already given him specifically for Derna.

Building in Benghazi has included new skyscrapers, hospitals, housing developments and a refurbished football stadium that last year hosted a friendly between Inter Milan and Atlético Madrid. Officials have talked in the past about turning the city into a version of "Dubai on the Mediterranean."

Belkacem tells the BBC he has accomplished more than any previous Libyan administration.

"Libya went through the Gaddafi era, 40 years of neglect and poverty," he said. "The interim governments [post-Gaddafi, based in Tripoli] wasted a lot of money without providing anything the people could touch. I have never made promises to the people. But I have provided them with what they need."

International human rights organisations have repeatedly accused the authorities in eastern Libya and Libyan Arab Armed Forces headed by Khalifa Haftar of serious abuses, including secret executions, arbitrary detentions and forced disappearances.

The Haftars and the Benghazi-based government deny the allegations. Belkacem told the BBC there was complete freedom of speech in eastern Libya.

Critics also say the Haftars have a top-down approach to development, with little public participation in planning decisions, and no transparency.

"There is absolutely zero accountability. We've never seen any financial statements of the Reconstruction Fund, for even the legal on-the-table disbursements of funds," says Claudia Gazzini from the International Crisis Group (ICG) think-tank.

Belkacem says the fund is independently audited and that all contracts are drawn up to high international standards. Dismissing concerns about transparency, he says: "What we've done in Derna was almost impossible. What we care about is the reality, what we do on the ground."

He agreed to show the BBC the audits. But he has not provided them, despite repeated requests.

Jalel Harchaoui, a Libya expert affiliated to the Royal United Services Institute think-tank in London, who has talked to some of the foreign partners awarded construction contracts. He says they are usually obliged to work alongside a private Libyan company linked indirectly to the Haftar family or other powerful political figures.

He says: "What those foreign companies say off the record, is that they do the overwhelming majority of the work and the Libyan partner is often almost an empty shell, in a context where the money is split very often on a 50-50 basis, which indicates that a lot of those facilities and bridges and towers are overcharged, twice as expensive.

"It's a form of overpricing within a context that is utterly opaque, and this is not some fairy coming from the sky that funds these reconstruction efforts. Everything is funded using the public wealth of Libya."

Belkacem Haftar denies the suggestion of corruption in reconstruction projects.

He has said the reconstruction funding was processed through the Central Bank of Libya, which operates on behalf of both the UN-recognised government in the capital Tripoli, in the west of the country, and the government in the eastern city of Benghazi.

"The Haftar authorities used Derna as a showcase for what they were pitching to the rest of Libya," says Gazzini from the ICG.

International efforts to reunite the country have included a proposal by Donald Trump's envoy, Massad Boulos, for a power-sharing deal with Saddam Haftar as Libya's president.

In Derna, there is no plan to rebuild the broken dams, so another disaster on the same scale is unlikely. But there is still a possibility of future flooding.

Gazzini says the authorities failed to take up offers of advice from international experts on ways to reduce the risk, for example by creating flood plains along the river which flows through the town.

"I would have expected a holistic project about how you manage the water flow," Gazzini says.

"But that did not happen. The Libyan side responded more to people's needs, was more interested in having a quick solution to the destruction of the city."

articles.title: 'Iran is not Cuba or Venezuela': Tehran warns it will not wait for US attack before responding
articles.summary: Iran has warned that it will not wait for the United States to launch an attack before responding, with deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi accusing
articles.body: Iran has warned that it will not wait for the United States to launch an attack before responding, with deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi accusing Washington of potentially using diplomacy to buy time for another military operation.Speaking to Iranian state television in an interview carried by Fars news agency, Gharibabadi said Tehran was preparing for three possible scenarios in its dealings with Washington: diplomacy, an economic blockade and military aggression.“Iran is not Cuba that you can blockade, nor is it Venezuela that you can force to surrender,” he said, adding that US forces had so far failed to achieve success through either an air or land blockade. He also claimed that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) was producing missiles with “new ranges”.Gharibabadi suggested that Washington could be exploiting diplomatic engagement to prepare the ground for another attack. He also said Iran remained in a state of war, rejecting the description of the current situation as “neither war nor peace”.“My personal belief is that from a legal perspective, we are still in a state of war and not in a neither-war-nor-peace situation,” he said.Tehran sets conditions for IAEA access to nuclear sitesGharibabadi said the IRGC would not allow the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) to inspect Iran's nuclear facilities until Tehran's conditions were met and the war had permanently ended.The remarks came after the UN nuclear watchdog called on Iran to restore access for inspectors to its nuclear facilities, including sites damaged during the conflict.“The agency’s request to visit Iran’s damaged nuclear sites is likely an assessment of the effectiveness of American weaponry,” Gharibabadi said.The deputy foreign minister, who previously served as Iran's ambassador to the IAEA, said Washington would first have to provide guarantees that Iran's conditions would be respected.“First and foremost, the US must provide the necessary guarantees that all of Iran’s conditions will be observed,” he said.Iran outlines demands for diplomatic agreementIn a separate televised interview with IRNA, Gharibabadi said the United States had repeatedly undermined Tehran's trust in diplomatic negotiations.“The US has shown its bad faith at least three times over the past year and a half. This shows that the US cannot be trusted at the diplomacy table,” he said.He cited the 12-day war and the 40-day war, which he said had taken place while negotiations were under way, as well as a 14-point memorandum of understanding that lasted less than two weeks.Iran's conditions for an agreement include a permanent end to the war on all fronts, the lifting of the US economic blockade and certain sanctions, including those targeting the oil sector, and a resolution of the issue of Iranian assets frozen abroad. Tehran also wants Washington to address the new military equipment and forces deployed in the region after the previous understanding.Gharibabadi said Iran had proposed a seven-day timeline for ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which was subsequently reduced to two days following consultations with mediators over the past two months.“This means the measures could be carried out within two days and ultimately lead to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz,” he said, adding that the proposal remained on the table.However, he said differences over the implementation of commitments continued to prevent an agreement. He maintained that the US would have to rebuild Tehran's trust if it wanted to pursue diplomacy.US carrier arrives in Middle East as regional tensions continueMeanwhile, the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, a US official cited by Al Jazeera claimed. It joins two other American carriers already operating within the US Central Command area of responsibility.Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed early on Sunday that it had struck a radar system at an American helicopter base in Bahrain, according to state-run IRNA. The US military's Central Command did not immediately comment on the claim.On Friday, Centcom said it had intercepted two Iranian drones heading towards Bahrain and denied an earlier Iranian claim that its forces had struck a US early-warning radar system there.Bahrain's military said on Sunday that its air defence systems had intercepted several Iranian projectiles before they reached their targets.Gharibabadi also criticised Washington's maximum-pressure sanctions policy, describing it as a failed approach that had not achieved its objectives during US President Donald Trump's first term.He acknowledged that sanctions affected ordinary Iranians but argued that their consequences for the global economy, energy and financial markets, as well as the US itself, were greater.You use AI every day. articles.title: Cancer 'sponge' tests for bad indigestion could be offered to more people
articles.summary: The "sponge on a string" tests can be done in GP surgeries, rather than hospitals, unlike endoscopy checks that use a small camera.
articles.body:
Some people with bad and persistent indigestion should be offered quick "sponge in the gullet" tests to check for oesophageal cancer, new draft guidelines for the NHS in England recommend.

The sponge tests can be carried out in GP surgeries in minutes, and are less invasive than hospital endoscopy checks that instead use a small camera to look inside the body.

They tests are already available in some places but could now be offered across England.

Heartburn or acid reflux can occur with a condition called Barrett's oesophagus that increases the risk of cancer in the long term.

It's thought between one and two adults in every 100 has Barrett's oesophagus, where cells have started to change. Most won't go on to develop cancer, but demand for NHS endoscopy is high, meaning some with the condition aren't checked as often as recommended.

The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) says the sponge tests, already offered in some places, could help give more patients peace of mind.

For the test, patients swallow a small dissolving capsule attached to a thread. Once in the stomach, it releases a tiny sponge. This collect cells from the lining of the gullet as it's gently pulled back out of the patient's mouth by the doctor.

Prof Jonathan Benger, chief executive of NICE, says sponge tests offer a "quick and less invasive" way to detect concerning changes, helping to identify people who should go on to have further tests and treatment.

Prof Peter Johnson, national clinical director for cancer at NHS England, said: "The NHS is always looking for better ways to get to the bottom of people's symptoms, and thousands have already benefited from this incredibly efficient test through pilots we have been running, so it's fantastic it is now being considered for roll out across the country.

"Many people have acid reflux, and having an easier way to check for changes in the lining of the oesophagus can make a big difference for patients, reducing the need for more complicated endoscopy tests and helping the NHS free up resources to find cancers at an earlier stage."

However, no diagnostic test, including endoscopy, identifies every case and people who receive an all-clear sponge test result should still be monitored in the long term, NICE adds.

The sponge tests can help detect oesophageal cancer and Barrett's oesophagus in people with reflux disease.

Final recommendations by NICE will be made in the new year.

Reflux can cause heartburn, which is a burning sensation in the middle of your chest, as well as an unpleasant sour taste in your mouth, caused by stomach acid.

Over time, this can damage the lining of the oesophagus.

A lax or weakened sphincter at the bottom of the oesophagus or food pipe, where it meets the stomach, can be part of the issue, allowing digestive juices to seep up the wrong way.

Being overweight, smoking and drinking alcohol can increase a person's risk of reflux.

articles.title: Black Friday and tax return scams - don't fall for these
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of scams are reported to HMRC - so it has advice on how to spot a fake request and refund.
articles.body:
This month's Black Friday and the tax return deadline at the end of January are both opportunities for fraudsters to scam you.

That's because people are more likely to expect emails, texts and other correspondence at this time of year.

Fraudsters will use the dates to impersonate genuine organisations and retailers by pushing victims towards fake websites to steal personal information.

Here's how to spot a scam and how you can avoid being caught out.

If you are self-employed or have more than one source of income you will need to file a tax return by the end of January.

Fraudsters seize on this deadline to blitz people with messages that look like they are official and from the UK's tax authority, HMRC.

Any such calls or messages should be ignored, but you can also check whether an email , text message or phone call claiming to be from HMRC is genuine.

"Reporting scams helps us shut them down and protect others," adds Lucy Pike, HMRC's chief security officer.

New figures from HMRC, shared with the BBC, show that it received 95,340 reports of suspected scams in the year to the end of October.

There were 900 reports of one specific scam which used emails containing a malicious attachment which directed customers to a fake gov.uk webpage designed to steal personal and financial information.

it never asks for personal or financial information by email or text message

it never leaves threatening voicemails about legal action or arrest

In the run-up to Black Friday you may be looking around for discounts, but fraudsters will impersonate genuine retailers to steal personal details or take payment for a product that will never be delivered.

Kirsty Adams, a fraud and scams expert at High Street bank Barclays, says make sure you pause before you buy.

"When you're scrolling on the sofa and a countdown timer starts ticking, or a deal pops up in your feed from an account that looks just like a brand you trust, it's easy to get swept up and pay before you've had a chance to check.

"No deal is worth rushing for. So take a moment before you buy."

The bank also advises doing these four things:

Pause and check , rather than being blinded by a countdown timer

Pay safely using a credit or debit card via a trusted payment service, not a bank transfer to a stranger

Open an official website or app yourself rather than clicking on links in emails, ads or social posts

Talk to a friend, family or your bank if you think something does not feel right, and calling your bank straight away if you think you've been scammed

articles.title: Founder of Guadalajara cartel dies in hospital after decades in prison
articles.summary: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo was convicted of the 1985 murder of a US drug enforcement agent and a Mexican pilot.
articles.body:
Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, the founder of one of Mexico’s first major drug cartels, has died in hospital at age 80.

Local security authorities said Felix Gallardo was transferred to a private hospital in the western city of Guadalajara two days ago but suffered multiple organ failure and died at about 2pm (20:00 GMT) on Sunday.

Felix Gallardo, a founder of the Guadalajara cartel, was convicted for the 1985 killing of a US drug-enforcement agent, a crime that made him one of the country’s most notorious traffickers.

Imprisoned since 1989, Felix Gallardo was held in a maximum-security prison in western Jalisco state, though his lawyers repeatedly sought house arrest on the grounds of his deteriorating health.

Rising to prominence in the 1970s, the former cartel kingpin was an architect of Mexico’s modern drug-trafficking trade, igniting a series of turf wars that have led to hundreds of thousands of deaths and disappearances in the ensuing decades.

Born in 1946 in Culiacan, Sinaloa, a northwestern state that would later become synonymous with narco-trafficking, he worked as a police officer and a bodyguard for a local governor. Later, he gained a reputation as a powerful criminal capo known as the “boss of bosses”.

Felix Gallardo and others set up their cartel in Guadalajara, the Jalisco state capital and a fast-growing economic powerhouse, becoming the first to move cocaine to the US on a massive scale and to forge an alliance with Colombian drug barons, including Pablo Escobar’s Medellin cartel.

His narcotics empire expanded in the 1970s and 1980s thanks to bribes that won protection from corrupt officials. His cartel also made innovations, such as using light aircraft to move drugs across the continent, supported by fellow kingpins like Rafael Caro Quintero.

His legal battles stretched across decades. Arrested in 1989, Felix Gallardo was sentenced to 40 years in prison on drug trafficking and weapons charges tied to the Guadalajara cartel.

While already jailed, he faced a separate prosecution over the 1985 kidnapping and murder of US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) agent Enrique “Kiki” Camarena and Mexican pilot Alfredo Zavala Avelar.

Camarena’s killing caused a diplomatic dispute with Washington, which pressured Mexico to arrest those involved.

In 2017, a federal court found Felix Gallardo guilty in the case and imposed a further 37-year sentence. He denied responsibility for the killings.

His rise and fall were portrayed on screen by Mexican actor Diego Luna in the 2018 hit Netflix series Narcos: Mexico.

Felix Gallardo suffered poor health in his final years and was blind in one eye, practically deaf, and unable to walk on his own by the time Spanish-language US network Telemundo interviewed him in prison in 2021. He maintained his innocence.

“Thirty-two years have passed,” he said. “That’s an eternity for a man who did not commit any crime.”

articles.body: When Lane Kiffin made the choice to leave Ole Miss late in the 2025 college football season for the LSU Tigers, one of his primary motivations was to coach in the College Football Playoff. Late in the 2026 college football season, he's about to make it two straight years of not coaching in the College Football Playoff. LSU took its fourth loss of the season on Saturday night, falling to the Texas Longhorns despite an atrocious performance from quarterback Arch Manning, and an overwhelming statistical advantage. It was the latest in a season full of similar losses, where LSU outplays the opposition and still loses. ESPN analyst Bill Connelly, creator of the SP+ ranking system, has an "postgame win expectancy" based on elements within a game that are most under team control: success rate, yards per play, explosives, field position, and turnovers. Losing this many close games is a function of randomness, to be sure, but when the randomness tilts this frequently in one direction, it's worth at least opening up the discussion that the coaches deserve some, if not most, of the blame. We won’t have senior days with two scholarship players." No "poor reflection" on the players, he says, but they're bad, and we'll have better ones in the coming seasons. How else is anyone listening supposed to take that? Including the players themselves. This is, remember, a roster that LSU spent an estimated $40-$50 million on, a level of spending that was a major factor in getting Kiffin to bolt for Baton Rouge. But then he brought it back to the roster again, saying, "Now also everything isn't built for the first year when you come in somewhere and I would tell you if we were undefeated right now, you know, you build things and they take a little bit of time..." Now that they're 6-4 and 3-4 in the SEC, he needs time to build the $40-$50 million roster up. Wonder what changed. He is right, however, to point out that these close games that come down to the final few seconds can hinge on one play or one bounce going a slightly different way. "Yes, we need to win games," Kiffin said. "But I also don't overreact. articles.title: Mexico's cartel 'godfather' convicted in American DEA agent's murder dies at age 80
articles.summary: The Guadalajara cartel boss convicted in DEA agent Enrique "Kiki" Camarena's murder died at 80, decades after the killing triggered Operation Leyenda.
articles.body: The Mexican cartel boss who helped build a drug empire supplying the United States and was convicted in the murder of Drug Enforcement Administration agent Enrique "Kiki" Camarena has died at 80. Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, known as the "boss of bosses," died Sunday in a Guadalajara hospital after suffering multiple organ failure, The Associated Press reported, citing Jalisco’s security ministry. He had been transferred from prison Friday. Felix Gallardo had been behind bars since 1989, according to The AP. JOHN KOUFOS: TRUMP’S ‘SHIELD OF THE AMERICAS’ COULD HELP DEFEND US FROM CARTELS His death comes more than four decades after Camarena’s abduction and torture, a killing that sparked the largest homicide investigation in DEA history, according to the agency. In 2017, a Mexican federal judge gave Felix Gallardo a 37-year prison term for the murders of Camarena and Mexican pilot Alfredo Zavala, Excélsior reported. The judge also ordered more than 20 million pesos in compensation for the victims’ families, roughly $1.18 million at the time. Camarena was heading to meet his wife for lunch on Feb. 7, 1985, when five men abducted him as he left the U.S. Consulate in Guadalajara, according to the DEA. One of the attackers identified himself as a Mexican law enforcement official. DRUG CARTEL KINGPIN AMONG TARGETS IN SWEEPING TRUMP CRACKDOWN ON ALLEGED MEXICAN CORRUPTION NETWORK The 37-year-old agent was never seen alive again. The DEA says Camarena was believed to have been tortured for two days before dying from a crushed skull. His body was discovered on March 5, 1985. His killing triggered Operation Leyenda, which the agency describes as the largest homicide investigation it had ever undertaken. Felix Gallardo was among the major Mexican crime figures arrested in connection with Camarena’s torture and murder, according to the DEA. ICE RENEWS HUNT FOR EL CHAPO'S LAST TWO FUGITIVE SONS WITH MASSIVE REWARD The agent, a Marine Corps veteran who joined the DEA in 1974, left behind his wife and three children. Felix Gallardo’s reach helped reshape organized crime in Mexico. A 2023 report released by Sen. Chuck Grassley’s office described the former police officer as having brought traffickers together into a large organization that became a blueprint for many of Mexico’s major criminal groups. EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE TRUMP'S CARTEL CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE OFFICIAL DETAILS PRESIDENT'S PRIVATE BRIEFINGS The Guadalajara cartel was among the first Mexican trafficking organizations to work with Colombian cocaine suppliers, according to a historical DEA publication. The agency said Felix Gallardo and Rafael Caro Quintero formed the cartel to ship heroin and marijuana into the United States before it prospered from the cocaine trade. Camarena’s legacy, meanwhile, lives on through the red ribbons worn each October in his memory as part of drug prevention efforts, according to the DEA. articles.title: Pete Buttigieg breaks with Democrats on student loan handouts, admits party ‘overtorqued’ on issue
articles.summary: Pete Buttigieg said the Democratic Party "overtorqued" on student loans, admitting that he struggles to justify loan forgiveness to non-college relatives.
articles.body: Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg admitted Sunday that he broke ranks with the Democratic Party on student loans, saying the party "overtorqued" the issue and may have dissuaded voters. During a "Pod Save America" interview, host Dan Pfeiffer remarked that many of the Democratic candidates who won in the midterm elections disagreed with the party on at least one issue, whether it be gun control or the role of oil and gas in energy. He asked Buttigieg whether he held any beliefs that ran counter to the mainstream Democratic Party. BERNIE SANDERS ADMITS DEMOCRATS FAILED WORKING-CLASS VOTERS ON ECONOMICS, DRIVING THEM TO DONALD TRUMP "In the 2020 campaign, I definitely staked out some positions that I still believe in that weren't always kind of popular in the party," Buttigieg said. "One thing is, I think...we really overtorqued on the student loan thing. As a party, I have a very hard time explaining to my relatives in Michigan who did not go to college why they should be paying for people who do." He added, "I believe there are ways to make sure that you come out of college debt-free. I believe college should be more affordable. I don't believe in like a magic wand to fix that for everybody who borrowed money." PETE BUTTIGIEG DISTANCES HIMSELF FROM BIDEN AMID 2028 TALK, SUGGESTS 'BUILD BACK BETTER' DOESN'T WORK Though Buttigieg told Pfeiffer that he doesn't believe in a "magic" fix for student loans, he previously served under President Joe Biden, who repeatedly attempted to cancel student loan debt, even after the Supreme Court ruled against his administration in 2023. His husband, Chasten Buttigieg, was also among those frustrated at the prospect of paying student loans after COVID-19-era loan relief was set to expire in 2022. Fox News Digital reached out to Buttigieg's organization, Win the Era, for comment. Veteran Democratic strategist Julian Epstein called the student loan forgiveness a scam and congratulated Buttigieg for having enough self-awareness to acknowledge it. JOE MANCHIN WARNS DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE GAINING GROUND AS DEMOCRATS REMAIN SILENT "Buttigieg shows an all-too-rare self-awareness for a Democrat elite on this issue. The student loan giveaway, also known as loan forgiveness, is a scam," Epstein told Fox News Digital. "It's welfare for the most privileged and elite amongst us that the working class has to help fund. It's Robin Hood in reverse, and it stands against everything the Democratic Party should be standing for." Another issue Buttigieg disagreed with the Democratic Party on was the two-party system itself. articles.title: ASEAN, China fall short of agreeing on South China Sea code
articles.summary: Southeast Asian leaders also denounce violence in Myanmar and extend ban on country’s leader attending bloc’s summits.
articles.body:
China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) have failed to conclude long-running negotiations on a code of conduct for the South China Sea during meetings in Manila, despite tentative agreement on about 80 percent of a draft, the Philippines’ foreign minister said.

“There is no conclusion yet,” Theresa Lazaro told reporters at the ASEAN summit on Sunday, adding that several key issues remain unresolved, including whether the code would be legally binding.

“The ASEAN countries plus China have also different views on how things are,” she added.

ASEAN and Beijing have been working on a code ⁠of conduct in the South China Sea, where they have overlapping claims, for more than two decades. The Philippines, as the current chair of the 11-nation association, had pledged to speed up the process and reach a deal by the end of this year.

Lazaro said she still hoped the code could be concluded under Singapore’s auspices, as the city-state takes over as chair next year.

Southeast Asian nations want the code to reflect international law, which some of them accuse China of ignoring. Beijing insists its actions have been lawful and professional.

China has laid claim to most of the South China Sea, clashing with the exclusive economic zones ⁠of Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam, making a functional code essential to keeping tensions from escalating and managing maritime encounters.

An international arbitration tribunal ruled in 2016 that China’s sweeping claims have no basis under international law, a decision Beijing rejects.

China and the Philippines, in particular, have faced off in a series of maritime confrontations in recent years.

The Philippines accuses Chinese ships of repeated ⁠aggressive actions inside its exclusive economic zone, including dangerous manoeuvres, firing water cannons and ⁠disrupting resupply missions. China accuses the Philippines of intruding on its territory.

Tensions escalated after Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr took office in 2022. Months of harsh words between the two countries over the sea preceded this weekend’s meetings.

Myanmar leaders still banned from summits

Separately, ASEAN extended a ban on Myanmar’s leader attending the bloc’s annual summits, saying the country failed to comply with a 2021 peace plan.

ASEAN leaders also decried Myanmar’s military and armed groups for continuing to attack civilians in the country’s long-running civil war.

Under the ban, Myanmar can be represented only by lower-level career diplomats, including at the summit in Manila. Myanmar was due to hold ASEAN’s rotating chair this year, but because of the civil strife, the role passed to the Philippines.

The stern rebuke followed a review of progress on the Five-Point Consensus for Myanmar, approved by ASEAN in April 2021 in a bid to ease the violence that erupted after Myanmar’s military seized power from the democratically elected government of Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi in February that year.

The military coup triggered widespread pro-democracy protests that were brutally quashed, leading to armed resistance and a civil war that has spread over much of the country.

In Manila, ASEAN leaders expressed “deep concern” over insufficient progress in implementing the plan and urged all parties to “stop targeted attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure”.

There are “still certain bombings and displacement of Myanmar people, so step-by-step, we give it to them, how they’re going to tackle this issue, and we’ll monitor that,” said Lazaro, who is also ASEAN’s current special envoy to Myanmar.

Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing, the former chief of the military, has made official visits to several ASEAN member states since assuming the presidency after elections in December and January, widely seen as having been rigged.

ASEAN has not discouraged those visits, but its leaders have emphasised that the peace plan remains “the main reference for addressing the political crisis in Myanmar”.
